pairs.why: A's teal hull gives saturated, toy-like colour closer to the bright real cards, while B's plain silver disc looks flatter and less designed.
B is a properly built saucer with volume, a rim of lights and an underside, so it reads as a solid object like the real cards, while A is a flat plate seen from above.
B is built like a real astronaut helmet, with side fittings and panel lines, matching the believable construction of the camera and vending machine, while A looks like a striped ball on a puck.
A is a featureless white sphere with a visor, while B has the structured, detailed build and soft finish of the real cards.
A's chunky, saturated forms and heavier mount are closer to the chunky binoculars and chair, while B's slim navy spyglass is more refined than the game's style.
B has a fuller painted scene, with a starry purple sky, rocks and soft crater shading, closer to the real cards' illustrated settings, while A is a sparse, flat CG render.
B's warm light, glowing door and steps, and charming storybook build match the inviting glow of the motel sign and lighthouse better than A's cold grey moonscape.
The two drawings are almost identical in build, colour and finish, so neither is meaningfully closer.
